feature.definition: A block `### F<n>` of the master that owns claims.

claim.definition: One falsifiable line `- [ ] ISC-<n>:` that closes on its probe.

task.definition: One atomic step of `tasks.md`, hanging on exactly one claim.

milestone.definition: A release named in the master's `## Milestones` block.

idea.definition: A story file under `specs/ideas/`, the stage before a spec.

stage.definition: Where a spec stands in its workflow.

workflow.definition: The ordered stages a spec type runs through, from `specs/workflow.md` or the default.

gate.definition: A condition a transition needs; two are fixed in every workflow: review before build, and every claim closed before done.

probe.definition: The command a claim closes on.

actor.definition: The neutral id in a file, `u:<8 hex>` for a person or `a:<kind>:<id>` for an agent.

agent.definition: A Claude Code session or sub-agent working a task, recorded as an `a:` actor.

chore.definition: The seventh spec type: `spec.md` only, review then build then done, no code review.

help.title: Help
help.subtitle: Spectant · the words, the workflows, the commands

about.body: Spectant reads the Markdown specs of your registered repositories and shows them on one board. The files are the only source of truth: the app keeps a small registry and its settings, and writes a file only when you move a card or tick a task.
about.shotBoard: The round board of a spec

lifecycle.label: How a feature moves, in eight stages

shape.title: Shape & plan
shape.sub: Files are written — no code yet

build.title: Build & finish
build.sub: Agents work in rounds — you hold the gates

what.idea: A story is shaped into a goal.
what.plan: Claims and fog are written down; the approach follows.
what.review: You release the spec for build.
what.build: Agents take claims and close them on their probes.
what.code-review: Code and security review of the tree.
what.close: Every claim is closed; the spec closes.

lifecycle.loopBlocked: blocked → back to build once you answer the question

moves.body: A spec moves through the stages of its type. On the board you drag its card, or open Move to… from the grip; core runs the same transition either way and either moves it or says, under the card, what is missing.
moves.chain: The stages of a feature, in the default order
moves.types: The workflow of each spec type

types.caption: The files each spec type has

commands.lead: Spec work starts in the AI chat with the Spec skill; the board shows the command a waiting card needs.
commands.caption: The commands of the Spec skill, as the stage table names them

list.spec-new: Turn a shaped story under specs/ideas/ into a spec folder.
list.spec-plan: Write plan.md: the how, locked in one question.
list.spec-tasks: Break the spec into tasks.md, one claim per task.
list.spec-review: Review the spec and record the reviewed mark, the gate into Build.
list.spec-implement: Work the tasks until every claim closes on its probe.
list.spec-code-review: Run the code and security review on the working tree.
list.spec-complete: Close the spec once every close condition holds.
list.spec-status: Phase, progress and claims of every spec in the repository.

start.lead: Three steps from the installer to the board.

steps.install: Install the binary with the one-line script from the README; it picks the build for your OS and architecture.
steps.register: Register a repository that has a `specs/` folder: `spectant add <repo>`.
steps.open: Run `spectant`, then open the workspace and its board: every spec and idea stands in its stage.

keyboard.lead: The same bindings as the shortcut sheet that ? opens.
